selection_rule: for the 6 questions run twice, the row of record is the pass that performed the ingest (max `seconds`) — see duplicate_remeasurements

duplicate_remeasurements.note: run twice (parallelised worker + sequential runner). The short pass finished in ~4-9 s (vs ~15-20 min) because the question's graph namespace was ALREADY POPULATED and the ingested point ids are deterministic (lme:<qid>:s<n>:t<m>), so it is an idempotent re-read, NOT an independent re-ingest. It shows the substrate is persisted and the measurement is stable on a populated graph; it is NOT evidence about extraction variance. Per-pass rows: 2578-probe-wave1-duplicates.jsonl.

extractor.note: resolve_extractor_provider() -> ('deepseek-direct', ['deepseek-direct','openrouter']) as recorded in the run log. RoutingModel exposes `provider`, not an `id`, so the per-row `extractor_model` field is null — the provenance is recorded here at report level.

db: dedicated falkordb-eval container (localhost:6380), one fresh graph namespace per question (probe2578w1_<qid>)

infra_incident.what: mid-wave throughput collapse: the client blocked indefinitely in a FalkorDB socket read (no timeout, no heartbeat, 0% CPU) while the extractor endpoint (1.0-1.2 s at a realistic payload) and isolated graph queries (0.07-0.68 ms) were both fast; the eval container was in a continuous active-defrag loop
infra_incident.mitigation: activedefrag disabled on the eval container; the wave-1 remainder was parallelised per question (independent graph namespaces) to bound wall-clock
